signals.title: Learning Molecular Representations from Cellular Phenotypes with Structure Preservation
signals.summary: Phenotypic drug discovery enables the discovery of functional relationships between molecular structures and cellular responses. However, existing multimodal representation learning methods often optimize cross-modal alignment without considering the intrinsic organization of chemical space, resulting in distorted molecular representations and loss of structural information.
signals.implication: High relevance to C2A2 operations; include in next leadership brief.
signals.long_summary: Phenotypic drug discovery helps uncover functional relationships between molecular structures and cellular responses. Current multimodal representation learning methods often prioritize cross-modal alignment but overlook the inherent organization of chemical space. This oversight can lead to distorted representations of molecules and a loss of crucial structural information. Addressing these issues is vital for enhancing the understanding of molecular interactions, which could directly impact drug discovery efficiency and effectiveness. For a community that seeks to remain informed about advancements in AI, this research underscores the importance of maintaining fidelity in molecular representation learning to improve connections between structure and function in drug development.

signals.title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation
signals.summary: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate human opinions, but prior work reports conflicting results: some studies find promising alignment with human survey data, while others find persona collapse and weak demographic sensitivity. We show that much of this conflict stems from conflating two distinct tasks.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: Large language models are being utilized to simulate human opinions, yet research shows conflicting results; some studies align well with human survey data, while others highlight issues like persona collapse and poor sensitivity to demographics. This discord is largely due to the conflation of two separate tasks in opinion simulation. Understanding these distinctions is vital for improving model performance and reliability in reflecting human perspectives accurately. Recognizing these differences will help the community stay informed about the capabilities and limitations of AI in representing human opinions.

signals.title: Every Wrong Answer Counts: Option-Level Psychometrics for LLM Multiple-Choice Benchmarks
signals.summary: Most multiple-choice question (MCQ) benchmarks evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) only by whether they select the correct answers. This binary scoring treats all incorrect responses alike, even though an LLM's preferences among incorrect options may contain systematic and useful information about its behavior and ability.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: Most multiple-choice question (MCQ) benchmarks for Large Language Models (LLMs) evaluate performance solely on whether the model selects the correct answers, using a binary scoring system. This approach ignores the nuances of incorrect responses, as an LLM's preferences among incorrect options can reveal systematic patterns that provide valuable insights into its capabilities and behavior. Recognizing the importance of this information can enhance the evaluation processes for LLMs, allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of their performance. This matters for our community because it emphasizes the need to adopt more nuanced evaluation methods that can better inform the development and application of AI technologies.
